title: Render-blocking a defer script or non-async module script
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

See
https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/608#issuecomment-1883688813

> My main concern is that it might be a bit too easy to block rendering on a `defer` (or `module` which is defer by default) script, and thus block until the timeout hits or until the full document is parsed. I'll file a spec issue.

In https://twitter.com/zcorpan/status/1744436513033630073 I wrote:

> Should we make this not work, or warn in Lighthouse? With module scripts being defer by default it seems a bit too footgun-y IMO.

@noamr replied:

> I think it works as intended… people have to explicitly mark those scripts render-blocking and doing so for an empty script would be very deliberate

me:

> How about copypasta a third-party non-empty script with the blocking attribute?

@noamr:

> As footguns go, this one is quite easy to spot (explicitly says render blocking) and more importantly to fix (add async). So IMO this is a matter of documentation rather than changing behavior.

For short documents, using render-blocking and defer together seems OK. So I'm not proposing that the spec should change to make `blocking=render` do nothing for defer or non-async module scripts. But maybe the spec should at least have a note or a warning about the implication of this combination, and developer tools / performance checks could have a warning at least when render-blocking has been active for a certain time.
